why_angle: The travel-kit pages cited give only the 100 Wh carry-on limit. None of them says that since 27 March 2026 the ICAO rules cap power banks at two per passenger and ban recharging them during international flights, or that Southwest bans seat-outlet recharging and Lufthansa Group bans in-flight use. Those rules change how every kit is packed: bank full before boarding, wall charger and cables in the carry-on, one bank under 100 Wh. This page states the rules from the ICAO, AirlineRatings and NBC pages.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Battery energy: UGREEN rates the 20,000 mAh bank at 72 Wh and the 25,000 mAh bank at 90 Wh (25,000 mAh × 3.6 V = 90 Wh). Both are under 100 Wh, the line above which an airline must approve a power bank in advance.
  • Laptop recharges: a 13-inch MacBook Air (M5) has a 53.8 Wh battery (Apple), so 72 ÷ 53.8 = 1.3 and 90 ÷ 53.8 = 1.7 full charges at rated capacity, before conversion losses.
  • Bank recharge time: both banks take 65 W in. At best, 72 Wh ÷ 65 W = 1.1 h and 90 Wh ÷ 65 W = 1.4 h, plus the slowdown near full.
  • Laptop port: the 25,000 mAh bank's C1 delivers 28 V × 5 A = 140 W. A 100W cable is limited to 20 V × 5 A = 100 W, which is why that kit uses the bundle with the 240W cable.
  • Laptop and phone on one charger: on the 100W charger, laptop on C1 and phone on C2 gets 65 W + 30 W (maker's table, Mighty Gadget). 65 W is below the 70 W a MacBook Air needs to fast-charge (Apple), but it matches the bank's 65 W input, so the bank can refill at full speed next to the phone.
  • Cart cost (UGREEN US, 2026-11-11): $54.99 + $60.22 = $115.21; $59.99 + $84.99 = $144.98; $44.98 + $60.22 = $105.20. The 20,000 mAh bank with two 100W cables ($60.22) costs $19.77 less than the bank alone ($79.99).

{kit:kit-laptop-phone-72wh} Laptop and phone traveler is the right kit for most people. You get a 100 W port for the laptop at the wall and on the bank, a 72 Wh bank that needs no airline approval, and both cables, for the lowest price of any kit with a 100 W wall charger. Put the laptop on C1, the phone on C2, and earbuds or a watch on C3. A third device cuts the laptop to 45 W, and USB-A only works paired with C1 or C2 (UGREEN).

{kit:kit-big-laptop-90wh} Bigger laptop, longer runtime is for a laptop that charges faster than 100 W, or for long days away from an outlet. Its 90 Wh is the most you can carry and still stay under 100 Wh. Use the 240W cable on the bank's C1 and the two 100W cables at the wall.

{kit:kit-uk-eu-65w} UK and Europe trips swaps the wall charger for a 65 W charger with US, UK and EU heads, so you don't need a separate plug adapter there. It suits a phone, a tablet, or a laptop that charges at 65 W or less. No Australian (Type I) head is listed, so Australia, New Zealand or China still need a plug adapter.

Power banks on planes: the 2026 rules change how you pack

From 27 March 2026, the ICAO rules for international aviation allow two power banks per passenger and ban recharging them during flights (ICAO). AirlineRatings summarizes the limits: under 100 Wh needs no special permission, 100–160 Wh needs the airline's approval in advance, over 160 Wh is banned, and power banks can't go in checked bags (TSA also requires them in carry-on). AirlineRatings adds that they can't go in overhead bins either. Airlines can be stricter:

  • Southwest: one portable charger per passenger from April 20, 2026, and it may not be recharged from in-seat power outlets (NBC New York, April 8, 2026).
  • Lufthansa Group (including SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings): since 15 January 2026, power banks may not be used or charged at any point during the flight. Passengers are told to use the seat's USB ports or power outlets instead (AirlineRatings, January 21, 2026).

What this means for any kit: charge the bank to full at the hotel or the gate. Pack the wall charger and both cables in your carry-on, not the checked bag, because on board the seat outlet charges the laptop or phone directly. Each kit here has one bank under 100 Wh, which meets Southwest's one-bank limit and the ICAO two-bank limit with no airline approval.

Not recommended

The 145W 25,000 mAh bank in UGREEN's bundle with a 100W cable 2-pack: it costs the same $84.99 as the 240W-cable bundle, but its 100W cables limit the 140 W port to 100 W. If you already own Anker's Prime 100W 3-port charger, keep the phone on C1. Anker's own output table shows USB-C2 and USB-A sharing 12 W + 12 W when used together.
